author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, on one page reached by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is requested, then the page lists each specialty by its stored name, exactly as recorded, with the veterinarians holding it
given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown by first name then last name, such as "Helen Leary"
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
given more specialties than one page of the veterinarian directory holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty appears on the single page, with no paging
given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each of them (edge case 3)
given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the specialty directory is opened, then the specialty is still listed, with no veterinarian beneath it (edge case 4)
given a clinic recording no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then the page opens and lists none (edge case 5)
given the specialty directory, when it is opened repeatedly, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same stable order (edge case 6)
given the navigation every page carries, when any page is rendered, then it holds no entry for the specialty directory, and the veterinarian directory carries no link to it

given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then it carries the same navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory as every page (REQ-SYS-001), and its wording is present in every supported language with none hard-coded (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: creating, editing, or deleting veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per the owner's decision)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory (deferred by the owner; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request)
listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
searching or filtering by specialty (NG-9 unchanged; the page takes no query)
translating specialty names (they appear by stored name)

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only page inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure; ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). It reuses existing patterns with one adjustment: a second lookup repository shaped like PetTypeRepository, because VetRepository cannot yield a specialty held by no veterinarian (edge case 4). The inversion, ordering, and full-name rules live in a new immutable value object, SpecialtyDirectory (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Value object). The controller stays rule-free (Web controller row): it reads, delegates to SpecialtyDirectory, and selects the view. Recorded in system-design: three new Contracts rows (SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController); REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository rows; the ordering and identity-matching invariant; the vet/ package-tree line; and a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. No ADR: the order choice is contained in this slice and a later slice may amend it (PRD Open Question). Covering code resolved by grep (weaker basis, IDE oracle not connected): VetRepository.findAll() @Cacheable collection read at VetRepository.java; PetTypeRepository ordered @Query at owner/PetTypeRepository.java; vetList.html layout usage with the menu key 'vets'.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController, package-private like VetController): binding target is none. The handler declares no @RequestParam, @ModelAttribute, or path variable, so the page takes no query (NG-9) and has no page parameter. Model: the SpecialtyDirectory only.

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> (not JpaRepository) and exposes one @Transactional(readOnly = true) read of all specialties ordered by name then id. No cache is declared; CacheConfiguration is unchanged.

SpecialtyDirectory is built by a static factory from (ordered specialty list, vet collection from VetRepository.findAll()). It holds an immutable, defensively copied, ordered list of per-specialty values, each carrying the stored specialty name and the ordered veterinarian full names (first name, space, last name). A vet holding no specialty contributes nothing.

Template vets/specialtyList.html uses fragments/layout with a menu key that matches no menuItem, so every page's navigation is unchanged and no nav item is active. layout.html and vetList.html are not edited: no entry and no link (owner decision). Render names with th:text only.

Wording: reuse existing bundle keys (e.g. specialties, name/vets) where they fit. Any new key must be added to every locale bundle in src/main/resources/messages/ (the REQ-LANG-002 build-time test compares bundle keys and scans templates for hard-coded text).

Double, domain boundary: SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses real Vet and Specialty instances with ids set. No double; these cover edge cases 3-6, the full-name format, and the omission of vets without a specialty.

Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests (@WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) + MockMvc, the sanctioned transport stand-in): hand-written doubles of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository registered as @TestConfiguration beans. Both are small Repository interfaces; return PageImpl for the paged overload. A @MockitoBean stub is not sanctioned for this new test.
Double, persistence: the SpecialtyRepository ordered read is exercised against the real H2 seed. Add a case to the existing ClinicServiceTests @DataJpaTest suite or a sibling @DataJpaTest; no double.

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository returning its values in name order
Thin package-private controller reading VetRepository and selecting a vets/ view
Layout fragment usage, full-name rendering via th:text, message-key wording
@WebMvcTest + MockMvc shape and Vet/Specialty fixture construction (Helen Leary / radiology); new test swaps @MockitoBean for hand-written doubles

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode. Specialty instances reached through cached Vet objects are not the instances SpecialtyRepository returns, so grouping by instance or Set membership silently drops every holding.
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping on Specialty id (system-design § Contracts invariant: match by specialty identity, never by instance); SpecialtyDirectoryTests builds vet-held and listed specialties as distinct instances sharing an id.

risks.risk: Specialty names are not unique in the schema and vets can share names, so a name-only sort is not stable across requests (edge case 6).
risks.mitigation: Order specialties by name then id and veterinarians by last name, first name, then id, inside SpecialtyDirectory (system-design § Contracts invariant). The repository's name ordering is not relied on as the stable-order guarantee.

risks.risk: Specialty directory path grows with specialties and holdings; the whole collection is read on every request (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: two whole-collection reads, one hash map keyed by specialty id, and a sort per specialty. The row records the size as unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Placing the inversion or ordering in SpecialtyController would be a fresh Web controller violation, not covered by the recorded deviation (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, In force note).
risks.mitigation: Controller only reads the two repositories, calls the SpecialtyDirectory factory, and returns the view name.

risks.risk: Stored specialty and veterinarian names are echoed into HTML (system-design § Threat Model, cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: th:text only, never th:utext; Thymeleaf default escaping stays on.

risks.risk: Vet data is served from the uncached-eviction 'vets' cache while specialties are read fresh, so an out-of-band vet change is not reflected (system-design § Open Questions 5).
risks.mitigation: Accepted as-is: no write path exists (NG-2). No cache is added for specialties and no eviction is introduced.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Design picks for the PRD open questions, recorded as triage decisions and amendable by a later slice: (1) specialties in name order with id tiebreak; veterinarians under each in last-name, first-name order with id tiebreak. (2) A specialty held by no veterinarian renders its name with nothing beneath it: no 'none' marker and no new message key for one. (3) No entry point: layout.html and vetList.html are untouched. The navigation test asserts that no rendered page (at least the specialty directory and the vet directory) carries an href to /specialties.html. The PRD Done-when bullet for REQ-SYS-001/REQ-LANG-002 is satisfied through the shared layout fragment and the existing bundle-key test. Test names come from the prd-entry test_names. The directory-logic cases belong in SpecialtyDirectoryTests; the page, the single unpaged page, and navigation belong in SpecialtyControllerTests.

semantic_surprise.note: The code does what its size suggests. SpecialtyDirectory.of groups holders by specialty id, not by instance, so the cached Vet's own Specialty copies match correctly. test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes. The MockMvc tests cover the route, the rendered names, six specialties on one unpaged page, and no nav href on either directory page. The only untested piece is rendering a specialty with no holders, which is an empty th:each and trivial.
